idiom_name: std::variant intents + std::visit reducer over value states + Qt signal or std::function subscriptions
implementation_notes: C++ supplies the pieces but no framework: intents are std::variant alternatives, the reducer is a pure function visiting the variant with an exhaustive overload set, states are value types (or std::shared_ptr<const State>) copied along the changed path, and the view subscribes through Qt signals or std::function slots and re-renders from the published snapshot. C++17 std::variant/std::visit gives the type-safe union and visitation, and const-correctness makes 'only the reducer creates state' partly compiler-checked, but immutability remains a convention because a non-const shared state can still be handed out. The classic form is warranted for Qt/ImGui-style UIs and for host-side harnesses that replay transitions; a single dialog with a few widgets is simpler with local widget state.
pitfalls: A std::visit overload set with a generic auto fallback silently swallows newly added intents; keep the visitor exhaustive so a new alternative fails to compile.
Lambdas connected to Qt signals capture this or state by reference; give the connection a context object or use weak ownership, or destroyed widgets keep receiving updates.
Sharing a non-const std::shared_ptr<State> between model and view recreates aliasing; publish shared_ptr<const State> or value snapshots.
Dispatching from several threads needs a policy (queue to the UI thread or a mutex); a reducer reading state while another thread dispatches is a data race.
